subject: Allocation of IP indemnity and evidence handover — counterproposal
messages:
From: Sally Nguyen <sally.nguyen@acme.io>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Initial proposal on IP indemnity allocation

Hi Jasmine / Kimberly,

Thanks for the draft MSA and order form. Our legal team reviewed the indemnity sections and wants to propose the following to close the loop quickly:

- Acme requests a full defense and indemnity for third-party IP infringement claims tied to the service.
- We propose a monetary cap equal to 12 months of fees for Order Form liability.
- Evidence handover: Acme needs copies of model input/output and request metadata within 14 days of notice for triage.

Given the scope of outputs involved, the defense-control clause is important for our procurement team. If Redwood is open to a limited carve for AI-generated derivative content, we can discuss an exception, but we need clarity on timing and preservation of logs.

Can you confirm whether Redwood will accept defense control for third-party claims or whether you prefer to accept liability but have Acme control defense? We want to avoid a prolonged back-and-forth — if you can send counter-redlines by next week we can route for signoff.

Best,
Sally
Director, Procurement
Acme Corp

[Attachment: acme_initial_redlines.pdf (pdf)]

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Sally Nguyen <sally.nguyen@acme.io>, Michael O'Leary <michael.oleary@acme.io>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Jan 2026 10:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial proposal on IP indemnity allocation

Hi Sally / Michael — thanks for the note and the redlines. Quick reply with Redwood's counterproposal below; attaching an annotated document with our suggested language.

Key points we can offer to move this forward:

1) Right to defend (Redwood): Redwood can accept defense control for third-party IP claims where the allegation concerns Redwood-delivered models or code. We will:
   - Provide prompt notice and lead the defense with counsel of our choosing.
   - Seek Acme's reasonable consent to settlements that impose obligations on Acme.

2) Settlement / reimbursement: If Acme chooses to step in and defend, Redwood will reimburse reasonable defense costs up to the indemnity cap.

3) Monetary cap: We propose a tiered cap — 12 months fees for claims arising from model inference (as you suggested) but allow negotiation for enterprise add-ons.

4) Evidence handover: We can commit to a 21-day window for an initial evidence bundle (request metadata + relevant logs). We need to limit PII exposure and will produce redacted artifacts or provide a secure review environment if required.

5) AI-generated outputs: We propose a narrow carveout that excludes claims solely based on user-provided content (i.e., where the infringement stems entirely from customer-supplied training data or prompts).

Attached: redlines_acme_v2.docx with inline suggestions and a short summary.

Next steps: Kimberly (legal) — can you review the attached and confirm whether the defense-control language and evidence timeline look workable? If we agree, Jasmine will send a mutual action plan and a DocuSign loop for the updated order form.

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwood.com

[Attachment: redlines_acme_v2.docx (docx)]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 17 Jan 2026 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial proposal on IP indemnity allocation

Jasmine / team — a few legal points to refine before we send back to Acme: 

- Defense control: I agree in principle to Redwood taking lead on defense for third-party IP claims tied to our models. We should add explicit cooperation obligations and a short cure window for Acme to propose alternate counsel (e.g., 10 business days) if there's a conflict.

- Settlement consent: "Reasonable consent" is vague — recommend we require Acme's consent for settlements that impose non-monetary obligations on them, but we reserve unilateral settlement ability for monetary-only settlements under the cap.

- Evidence production: 21 days is OK as an initial bundle. Add a clause limiting the scope to logs we retain in the ordinary course and require a protective order for sensitive data. For on-prem customers this is more complex; for hosted customers we can provide a secure review environment rather than full raw dumps.

- AI output carveout: Narrow the carve strictly to customer-supplied training data or prompt text. Do not carve outputs where infringement arises from our model's pre-trained weights or proprietary layers.

- Cap drafting: Suggest we use a headline cap tied to the Order Form; avoid language that splits calculation across services.

I will prepare a short legal memo and mark-ups for the MSA and order form. Jasmine — once I share the memo, can you include procurement and sales in the mutual action plan so we can track signoffs?

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

[Internal note: preserve the thread for signature chain and procurement approvals]

From: Michael O'Leary <michael.oleary@acme.io>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Sally Nguyen <sally.nguyen@acme.io>
Date: Mon, 19 Jan 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Allocation of IP indemnity and evidence handover — counterproposal

Thanks for the detailed responses. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Defense control: Acme is willing to accept Redwood leading defense for third-party IP claims, provided Redwood acknowledges Acme's right to direct defense if Redwood refuses to assume defense within 14 days of notice.

- Settlement consent: Acme needs a clear escalation for settlement approvals; proposed: Acme has final say on non-monetary commitments that materially impact our operations.

- Evidence timeline: The 21-day initial bundle is workable, but we need an SLA on a fuller evidence set (e.g., 60 days) for deeper investigation. Also request location and retention period for logs to be stated in the order form.

- Cap: We're okay with the 12 months fee cap as a starting point but would like to include an insurance-first clause if Redwood carries a cyber/tech E&O policy that could respond for covered claims.

If you can incorporate Kimberly's memo and our clarifications into a short mutual action plan (dates + owners), we can circle back to procurement and legal for final signoff.

Best,
Michael O'Leary
Head of Vendor Contracts, Acme Corp

[Link: HubSpot deal ACME-2026-014]

Michael / Sally — thanks, all — good alignment. Attached is a short mutual action plan and timeline. Summary of agreed items for the plan: 

- Legal mark-ups: Kimberly to deliver clean mark-ups for MSA and Order Form (due: 2026-01-21).
- Evidence SLA: Redwood to provide initial bundle within 21 days, fuller dataset in 60 days (subject to protective order).
- Defense control: Redwood will assume defense within 14 days of notice or Acme may step in; settlements that impose non-monetary obligations on Acme require Acme consent. 
- Cap & insurance: Use 12 months fees as headline cap; include an "insurance-first" carve where Redwood's applicable E&O responds before indemnity is tapped.
- Procurement signoff: Acme procurement to confirm by 2026-01-28.
